solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hopeful, I'm first to break attachment to bottle

indicators.note: the clue's pieces break into the bottle attachment, splitting it open

parts.note: an optic is the measuring device fixed to an upturned spirit bottle in a bar
taken as the letters IM
1st, written as I plus ST

explanation.surface: A cheerful drinker hopes to break into a bottle with its pub measure attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, with the numeral read as the letter I; an optic is the spirit measure fixed to an upturned bottle behind a British bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hopeful expects things to turn out well, which is the outlook of a positive thinker.

clue.text: Twelfth Night character actors in Othello part

indicators.note: only a part of the words actors in Othello is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Seems to ask which Twelfth Night role the actors in an Othello production play.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'actORS IN Othello'; 'part' signals taking just that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Orsino of Illyria is a leading figure in Shakespeare's comedy, lovesick for Olivia.

clue.text: Cut right into fish

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes into the fish's name

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: An angler's instruction to slice straight into a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch dug or cut into the ground.

clue.text: What will find you the right place? A degree will

definitions.text: What will find you the right place?

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
one's will is one's wish or choice, a preference

explanation.surface: Asks what gets you to the right place, then quips that a university degree will.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sentence is the wordplay: MA (a degree) followed by PREFERENCE (will, as in free choice).
explanation.definitionFit: A grid reference on a map pinpoints a location so a reader can find it.

clue.text: Old ruler has unruly head of hair

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of has are put out of order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old monarch with a mop of untamed hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges HAS to SHA; 'head of hair' adds H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran (Persia), deposed in 1979.

clue.text: Show houses feel occasionally vulgar

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so the picked letters sit within the verb

parts.note: to indicate is to show or point out

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means every other one

explanation.surface: An estate agent's show homes are judged rather tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes E and L, the second and fourth letters of 'feel'; 'houses' puts them inside INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vulgar is coarse and lacking in good taste, which is improper or indelicate.

clue.text: A mother's boy

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a lad who clings to his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'mother's boy' is the trap: A + DAM, then 's links to the definition 'boy'. Wittily, the first man had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, and also the first man in Genesis.

clue.text: One who, in France, runs into Welshman for a drink

indicators.note: these pieces run into the Welsh name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David
the Roman numeral I is one
qui is French for who
R is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Frenchman bumps into someone from Wales, and they go for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A daiquiri is a cocktail of rum, lime juice and sugar.

clue.text: Lane concealed in West Irish town

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the film star's first name

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood actress
La is an abbreviation for Lane in street addresses
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A country lane tucked away somewhere in the west of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks geographical but is the Hollywood actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Malahide is a coastal town north of Dublin, home to a famous castle.

clue.text: They may tick when passed around

definitions.text: They may tick when passed around

parts.words: They may tick when passed around
parts.note: the second hands on a clock sweep round the face, ticking as they go; the surface suggests a sheet passed around for people to tick

explanation.surface: Suggests a register or form handed round for people to tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweep hands are the long second hands that sweep continuously round a clock face.

clue.text: Following crook is all you can take

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
crook is British and Australian slang for unwell

explanation.surface: Following a criminal is about as much as anyone can stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but is the adjective meaning ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Having one's fill means having as much as one can manage or tolerate.

clue.text: Howl after cuts (despite using this?)

indicators.note: one word cutting into another splits it open and sits inside

parts.note: to howl is to scream
having, as in having eaten, means after eating

explanation.surface: Someone yells after nicking himself shaving, despite the foam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' works as in 'having eaten' = after eating; the whole clue also describes the scene of a nick while shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather applied before a razor is meant to stop nicks, yet the shaver still howls at cuts.

clue.text: One poaching squid?

definitions.meaning: someone who nicks, that is steals, such as a poacher
playfully read as quid: British slang for a pound, as is quid

explanation.surface: Describes someone poaching a cephalopod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squid' is not the sea creature: the question mark flags it as S + QUID, the pound coin, which a nicker also is in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief nicks things, and nicker is also slang for a pound sterling.

clue.text: While singer captures hearts, I hate it

indicators.note: the singer holds the card-suit letter inside

parts.note: an alto is a singer in the voice range below soprano
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A singer wins hearts while someone else groans in dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are concessive conjunctions meaning though or even if.

clue.text: Most of wine goes up in flames, making Spaniards' point

indicators.note: the reversed wine sits inside the word for flames

parts.note: flames are fire

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading backwards
most of a word means losing its last letter

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resin-flavoured wine

explanation.surface: Pictures a bottle of wine going up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the wine's last letter and 'goes up' reverses what remains, giving NISTER inside the flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Finisterre is a headland on the coast of Galicia in north-west Spain.

clue.text: One snooker problem worked out again

definitions.meaning: a ..., a ball blocked by another so it cannot be potted
found out or discovered once more

explanation.surface: A snooker player's tactical difficulty finally gets solved again.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part splits as RED IS COVERED, a snooker player's predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To rediscover is to find again something once lost or forgotten.

clue.text: Disheartened lad splits from poor ex

indicators.note: the shortened lad splits the little word for from by sitting inside it

parts.note: of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter goes

parts.note: lame means poor or feeble, as in a lame excuse

explanation.surface: A dejected young man breaks up with a hard-up former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes the middle letter, leaving LD; 'from' is the small word 'of', as in 'a man of Kent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A former lover or sweetheart is someone you once carried a torch for.

clue.text: Bill entered by more than one Liberal canvasser

indicators.note: the bill has the liberals come into it

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck up on a wall
L abbreviates Liberal, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: An election canvasser visited by several Liberal Party members.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollster canvasses public opinion by surveying people.

clue.text: Roomy if turned into bathroom?

indicators.note: the turned word goes into the bathroom phrase

parts.note: the question mark lets bathroom stand for a loo setting, the room a loo is set in

indicators.note: turned round means read in reverse

explanation.surface: Asks whether a roomy space could be converted into a bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if turned' gives FI, put into LOO SETTING (the setting of a loo, flagged by the question mark).
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-fitting clothes are cut generously, with plenty of room inside them.

clue.text: Look sullen after officer offers excuse

indicators.note: the sulky look comes after the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: CO is Commanding Officer
to pout is to push out the lips sulkily

explanation.surface: A sulking soldier offers a weak excuse to an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion, a feeble way of dodging responsibility.

clue.text: Prisoner's uniform found in gym, causing trouble

indicators.note: the prisoner and uniform are found within the gym lesson

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class
a lag is a convict, especially an old lag
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A prisoner's outfit turns up in the gym and causes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague someone is to pester or torment them persistently.

clue.text: Eccentric suppressing proper bliss

indicators.note: to suppress here is to hold down inside, so the eccentric word contains the other

parts.note: fey means whimsical or unworldly
licit means lawful, proper

explanation.surface: A quirky person keeps a lid on a sense of rightful joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is intense happiness, a synonym of bliss.

clue.text: Document that is sent to press

indicators.note: the abbreviation is sent next to the word for press, placed in front

parts.note: sc., scilicet, is Latin for namely or that is
to roll is to press flat, as with pastry

explanation.surface: A document that gets sent off to the printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests printing but means ROLL; 'that is' is the Latin abbreviation SC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled parchment bearing writing is an old form of document.

clue.text: Way into mine's been doomed to not open

indicators.note: not opening means losing the first letter

parts.note: to have had it is to be doomed, finished

explanation.surface: A mine's entrance has been condemned to stay shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Mine's been doomed reads as 'has had it'; HAD IT without its opening H gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage driven into a hillside to reach a mine.

clue.text: Puts on a show while holding court

indicators.note: the word for while holds the court abbreviation inside

parts.note: as means while, as in as I was walking

explanation.surface: A performer stages a show while holding court among admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform or put on a theatrical show.

clue.text: Lullaby somehow led child to get into rock

indicators.note: the shuffled letters and the child go inside the rock

parts.note: a crag is a steep rocky outcrop

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of led are rearranged by some means

parts.note: a son is a child

explanation.surface: A lullaby somehow coaxed a child into the rocking cradle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns LED into DLE; with SON, they 'get into' CRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle song is a gentle tune sung to lull a baby to sleep.

clue.text: Make a seabird's sound

indicators.note: the noun sound points to how the bird's name is said

parts.note: the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle

explanation.surface: Seems to ask you to imitate a gull's cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a cry but signals a word said the same: ERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to make money through work.

clue.text: Measure heart's inner beat?

indicators.note: inner places the beat inside the word for heart

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
musical beat is time, as in keeping time

explanation.surface: Asks how to measure the inner rhythm of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart's inner beat' suggests a pulse, but the heart is a centre and the beat is musical time.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length in the metric system, one hundredth of a metre.
